paper.title: Hierarchy-boosted funnel learning for identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes a hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework that integrates unsupervised and supervised learning to efficiently identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL), circumventing large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations. It uses unsupervised clustering on a high-throughput dataset to narrow the search space, performs low-cost phonon-elasticity-thermal (PET) model-based high-throughput calculations on selected clusters to build a labeled local database, trains a CatBoost classifier for direct prediction of ultralow κL, and conducts interpretable SHAP analysis to uncover structural descriptors governing κL modulation—especially discovering Lmin as a new factor influencing structural anharmonicity and phonon lifetime.

task.task_name_raw: identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
task.objective: Identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL) for potential thermoelectric applications.
output_goal: list of candidate semiconductors with ultralow κL
discovery of new factor (Lmin) governing structural anharmonicity

evidence.text: Here, we propose a novel hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework, which is successfully applied to identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL).
We then apply this HiBoFL framework to efﬁciently identify semiconductors with ultralow κL as shown in Fig. 1b.

As a compelling demonstration, this framework has been successfully applied to identify semiconductors with ultralow κL, which circumvents large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations without clear objectives.

stages.stage_name_raw: obtaining material dataset from Materials Project database
stages.stage_goal: Acquire initial theoretical dataset of semiconductors for screening.

evidence.text: Initially, we start by acquiring all the materials from the MP database based on its API, resulting in a total of 1,54,718 entries saved in a JSON ﬁle as the Python dictionary object.

stages.stage_goal: Filter raw MP dataset using thermodynamic, electronic, structural, and elemental constraints to form first-level dataset.

evidence.text: Ultimately, through excluding the materials containing hydrogen, lanthanides, and actinides, and conducting structural analysis, we further obtain 2675 three-dimensional (3D) crystal structures without calculation errors. These materials constitute the ﬁrst-level dataset for our in-depth investigations.

stages.stage_name_raw: unsupervised learning for clustering materials with similar κL
stages.stage_goal: Group first-level dataset into clusters based on compositional and structural similarity to identify problem-specific clusters likely containing low-κL materials.
stage_output: problem-specific clusters C1 and C2 (704 materials)

evidence.text: K-means clustering41,42 is then employed to identify materials with similar κL, which is visualized in a low-dimensional space using t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE)43, and problem-speciﬁc clusters are selected based on similarity design rules to form the second-level dataset.

Since the materials with a high likelihood of possessing relatively low κL tend to group into the two clusters of C1 and C2, the exploration scope for ﬁnding materials with low κL is reduced from 2675 materials to 704 materials, narrowing by approximately three-quarters. As a result, these two problem-speciﬁc clusters (C1 and C2) further constitute our second-level dataset.

stages.stage_name_raw: high-throughput calculation of κPET using PET model
stages.stage_goal: Assign ultralow κL labels to materials in C1/C2 via low-cost empirical PET model to establish labeled local database.
stage_output: 661 labeled materials with κPET values at 300 K

evidence.text: Based on the PET empirical equation within the high-throughput framework, we derive the κPET values at 300 K ignoring the anisotropy for materials in the second-level dataset, while excluding structures that do not satisfy the mechanical stability criteria. The basic information and corresponding κPET values of the resulting 661 materials are then stored in a local database using MongoDB64, serving as a valuable repository to retrieve data and prioritize detailed theoretical and experimental investigations.
evidence.section: HTC of problem-speciﬁc clusters for statistical analysis and material discovery

stages.stage_goal: Screen candidates with κPET ≤ 2 W/mK and select top-ranked unreported materials (Cs2SnSe3, Cs2GeSe3) for in-depth validation.
stage_input: experimental literature on known low-κL materials
stage_output: list of candidate materials with potential TE applications (Table S2)

evidence.text: Of particular note is that nearly 70% of these semiconductors exhibit the κPET values no greater than 2 W/mK (left panel in Fig. 4a), with a considerable portion of these materials remaining unreported to date. stages.stage_name_raw: training CatBoost classifier on labeled local database
stages.stage_goal: Train interpretable supervised classification model to predict ultralow κL (κPET ≤ 2 W/mK) directly from descriptors.

evidence.text: We perform ensemble learning on the labeled local database for directly classifying ultralow κL, training a robust CatBoost classifier45.

After labeling the materials in the second-level dataset based on our HTC framework to obtain the local database, we develop interpretable supervised classiﬁcation models to predict ultralow κL for efﬁciently by-passing the complex ab initio calculations... evidence.text: The interpretable analysis of the pre-trained model based on the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method46–48 further reveals the inﬂuence of important descriptors on ultralow κL.
